sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The trial of Stephen Yaxley-Lennon, also known as Tommy Robinson, has opened at Southwark Crown Court. Outlets disagree on his age, with the BBC stating he is 43 and The Guardian reporting 42. Prosecutor Ben Holt told the jury that Yaxley-Lennon harassed Daily Mail journalists Andrew Young and Jacob Dirnhuber after they reported on his holiday in Cyprus following the July 2024 Southport attacks. sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Amazon Web Services released a tool called TorchNeuron on Monday, allowing AI startups to easily move apps onto Amazon's Trainium chip by changing one line of configuration. The tool works with PyTorch and challenges Nvidia's dominant software advantage.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Nvidia's CUDA software has made its hardware the default choice for AI. TorchNeuron aims to remove this lock-in, giving developers a way to use Amazon's cloud and custom chips while potentially lowering costs.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Covid inquiry sixth report found that government action to protect care homes came too late, resulting in over 43,000 recorded deaths. Additionally, GPs imposed unlawful blanket do not resuscitate orders.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Long-standing sector weaknesses, such as high staff vacancies, zero-hours contracts, and fragmented services, undermined the pandemic response. This exposed residents to severe health declines, caused deep distress among care staff, and strained mental health.

gist: Nini Rodgers was a historian of Ireland’s involvement with slavery and abolition.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Historian Nini Rodgers died at the age of 86. Throughout a four-decade career at Queen’s University Belfast, she taught thousands of students and championed part-time night degrees. In 2007, she published her major work, Ireland, Slavery and Anti-Slavery: 1612-1865, challenging Ireland's self-image regarding the transatlantic slave trade. She was the daughter of Marie and the poet WR Rodgers, and partner to the late historian Jack Gray.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Rodgers's research meticulously unmasked the reality of Ireland's involvement in slavery, replacing comforting fables with precise knowledge. She also shaped generations of historians and brought higher education to new kinds of people through her commitment to part-time students.

timeline.text: It’s a bird, it’s a plane … it’s a robo-puffin?

gist: MIT and EPFL engineers designed a flying and swimming robot inspired by diving birds.
The lightweight robot can smoothly transition from water to air using flexible wings.
This technology may enable affordable data collection in dangerous aquatic regions.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Engineers at MIT and EPFL created a lightweight flapping-wing aerial-aquatic vehicle weighing under 300 grams. It uses a waterproof motor, flexible wings coated with nanoparticles, and a motorized tail. Tests in a water tank and Lake Geneva showed the robot can successfully transition from swimming underwater to flying in the air.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Moving through both air and water is difficult because water is much denser than air. This robot overcomes this challenge without needing feet. It could provide a cheaper way for oceanographers and marine biologists to sample hazardous aquatic areas.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The research team aims to design wings that can both turn and flap. They also plan to test the robot in turbulent conditions like choppy water and windy air before deploying it for ocean science research.

gist: Firefighters and control room staff were stretched dangerously thin during this summer's wildfires.
A parliamentary report revealed that firefighters struggled with water supplies and poor preparation amid drought.
A summit is being held to address climate resilience and future wildfire preparedness in Wales.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: This summer's record-breaking heat and drought fuelled serious wildfires across the UK. Fire services faced unprecedented demand, with crews managing multiple major fires at once and control rooms handling thousands of calls. Firefighters reported severe shortages of staff, appliances, proper equipment, and water supplies due to low pressure and depleted natural sources.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The crisis exposed critical weaknesses in the UK's resilience and preparation for extreme weather. Experts warned that firefighters and the public were knowingly put at risk as climate breakdown increases the frequency and severity of wildfires, placing an unsustainable burden on emergency services and water networks.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Leaders and key partners are gathering for a climate change and resilience summit in Merthyr Tydfil to develop future actions. A UK wildfire conference is also scheduled in Leeds, while MPs have called on the government to establish statutory responsibilities for water companies during major fire incidents.

quotes.text: Firefighters cannot fight fires without water.

sections.text: Outsourcing firm Capita took over administering the Civil Service Pension Scheme in December 2025 and inherited a large backlog. gist: Websites across Europe take systems offline ahead of critical PHP updates.
Two critical vulnerabilities with severity ratings of 9.2 out of 10 affect PHP.
Global cyber-security agencies urge organisations to apply patches or isolate systems.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Finnish and Dutch governments took down websites ahead of a planned software update to the PHP programming language. Two critical vulnerabilities affecting versions from PHP 5 onwards were identified, prompting cyber-security agencies worldwide to issue warnings and advise organisations to apply fixes or take their websites offline.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: PHP powers a massive portion of the internet, including WordPress sites and hosting platforms. The vulnerabilities could allow unauthenticated remote code execution, letting hackers install malware, take down websites, or run their own code on affected servers.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Security patches are expected to be released, and organisations are urged to rapidly adopt the updates. Cloudflare reported seeing early attacks emerging, while experts warn that finding every instance of PHP running will be a major challenge.

timeline.text: 'Targeted' attack on much-loved MP leaves Australian town heartbroken

gist: Independent MP Helen Haines was severely injured in a targeted car attack in Wangaratta.
The community and national leaders expressed shock and support following the deliberate incident.
A local man appeared in court facing multiple charges as police consider further action.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Independent federal MP Helen Haines was struck by a car in a targeted and deliberate attack outside her Wangaratta office on Monday afternoon. She sustained severe injuries requiring both legs to be amputated after being airlifted to Melbourne. A local man was arrested at the scene after being pinned down by a witness, and appeared in court facing charges including intentionally causing harm, with police considering further charges such as attempted murder.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The tragedy has left the rural Victorian town of Wangaratta and the wider Australian community in profound shock. Haines is widely regarded as a well-liked, dedicated representative known for championing anti-corruption reform and regional infrastructure, making the violent incident deeply unsettling for locals who view her as a community fixture.

fivew: An independent MP was struck by a car in what police describe as a targeted attack.
Outside an office in Wangaratta, Victoria.

sections.text: The allegations involve serious criminal claims and links between far-right figures and political circles. Ross served as chief executive of Turning Point UK and had advised politicians, raising scrutiny over connections between fringe political groups and mainstream parties.

sections.text: The Conservative party suspended Ross with immediate effect pending an investigation. Additionally, Police Scotland announced they will be reviewing and assessing the documentary footage for any criminality.

gist: Severe flaws undetected for years in PHP were uncovered using artificial intelligence.
Governments and organisations globally rushed to patch systems or take affected websites offline.
Experts warned that attacks may increase as technical details are made public.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Researchers at cyber-security firms Calif and Wiz used artificial intelligence to uncover serious vulnerabilities in PHP. The programming language underpins websites including Wikipedia and WordPress. Following an online leak of the discovery, developers issued emergency patches, whilst authorities worldwide urged immediate updates or temporary site shutdowns.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The flaws could permit attackers to seize unauthenticated control of web servers and extract sensitive information. The alert caused international disruption, leading governments, councils and platforms such as Wikimedia to suspend pages temporarily. Amazon reported experiencing multiple attack attempts before public disclosure.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Experts expect further exploitation attempts in coming weeks as technical details circulate. Officials urged organisations to patch systems promptly or suspend affected pages, while web users were advised to watch for password-change requests and phishing messages.

stories.standfirst: From George Balanchine to the Rockettes, the US magazine regularly ran lavish photo spreads dedicated to dance, with the myriad ways people moved their bodies holding up a mirror to the changing times

articles.title: Proms, parties and gender politics: amazing photos from American dancefloors – and what they tell us about a changing nation
articles.standfirst: From George Balanchine to the Rockettes, the US magazine regularly ran lavish photo spreads dedicated to dance, with the myriad ways people moved their bodies holding up a mirror to the changing times

timeline.text: Proms, parties and gender politics: amazing photos from American dancefloors – and what they tell us about a changing nation

gist: A new Taschen book compiles dance-themed photographs from the historic Life magazine archive.
The images chronicle shifts in American culture, gender politics, race relations and individualism.
Featured moments include Cold War tensions, iconic performers, high school proms and global dance crazes.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Taschen published LIFE. Let’s Dance, a book drawing on dance photography from the archive of Life magazine, which ran weekly between 1936 and 1972. The collection covers social dancing across ballrooms, clubs, proms and parties, showcasing styles from the waltz and lindy hop to the twist. It also documents renowned performers, including George Balanchine, Margot Fonteyn, Rudolf Nureyev, Whitey’s Lindy Hoppers, the Rockettes, and actors filming the movie musical Can-Can.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The archive reflects broader shifts in twentieth-century American society. The transition from structured couple dancing to freeform movement captured emerging gender politics and individualism. Photographs also traced shifting racial dynamics, from segregated venues and newly desegregated schools to the mainstream adoption of Black and Latin American styles. In addition, dance intersected with Cold War tensions, from Soviet premier Nikita Khrushchev criticising Hollywood routines to comparisons between American and Soviet schools.

fivew: Publisher Taschen released the book featuring work from Life magazine's photographers.
A collection of dance-themed photographs from the Life magazine archive has been published in a book.

The archive reflects major twentieth-century American social changes, gender politics, race relations and Cold War tensions through dance.

timeline.text: Just because Tesla’s Optimus is in production doesn’t mean it’s actually ready

gist: Tesla has begun early production of its Optimus humanoid robot in Fremont, California.
Significant software and hardware challenges remain, particularly regarding robot hands and AI capabilities.
Elon Musk expects customer deliveries around late 2027, though independent experts are skeptical.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Tesla announced it has begun early production of its Optimus humanoid robot on its high-volume line in Fremont, California. CEO Elon Musk stated that the company is ramping up manufacturing before perfecting the robot's hands, software, reliability, and durability.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Although production is underway, experts point out that lacking necessary software and durable hardware presents a major problem. Tesla must still gather training data by building thousands of practice robots and integrating new chips.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Tesla plans to build a fleet of robots to practice tasks and intends to integrate the AI5 chip around April 2027. Musk expects customer deliveries could begin around the end of 2027.

fivew: Tesla began early production of its Optimus humanoid robot.
To move toward manufacturing the robot at scale despite ongoing software and hardware challenges.

timeline.text: Googlebooks just aren’t ready

gist: Googlebook laptops feature excellent hardware but are held back by immature operating software.
Prices across the initial lineup range from $899 up to $1,299 depending on the manufacturer.
Reviewers advise against purchasing the current devices until the software improves significantly.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Reviewers tested the first generation of Googlebooks from manufacturers including Acer, Dell, HP, Asus, and Lenovo. While praising the premium builds, screens, keyboards, and battery life, testers found the operating system buggy, limited, and akin to an unpolished beta.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: At prices starting from $899, these laptops demand high-end expectations. However, software limitations such as poor app support, missing features, and frustrating tablet orientation bugs make the current lineup a difficult recommendation.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Google continues to update and improve the operating system, but reviewers advise consumers to wait until the software catches up with the hardware before buying.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: 1Password introduced 1Password for Agents, a new feature enabling AI agents to sign into accounts securely without seeing or handling actual passwords. The system uses a unique digital key to verify the agent's identity and requires device approval from the user.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: As AI agents perform more tasks requiring logins, traditional credential sharing poses security risks. This tool provides a trust layer, preventing agents from gaining permanent access to accounts while maintaining convenience.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The feature is designed to work with various popular AI agents, and additional integrations and partner support are expected to come.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: The Atari VCS software store is shutting down on February 1st, 2027, following years of delays and name changes. Owners can continue adding software until January 31st, 2027, and previously downloaded apps and games will remain usable.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The closure marks the end of the retro-inspired Linux-based mini PC platform's online store functionality, shifting how users will manage and access software libraries.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Atari plans to release an OS update to migrate functionality to local machines and remove dependencies on Atari infrastructure. The company also intends to release an Atari Home Brew app for community-developed games.

fivew: The Atari VCS software store is shutting down and the platform is being retired.

gist: Nirva raised $33M in total funding for its new jewelry-like AI pendant.
The device is designed to passively listen only to the wearer's speech.
Orders begin in November with shipments targeted by the end of the year.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Startup Nirva announced a $25 million pre-Series A round, adding to an earlier $8 million raised this year, bringing its total raise to $33 million. Founded in 2025, the company is building an eight-gram pendant that can also be worn as a bracelet and lasts up to three days on a single charge.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Privacy is a major concern for ambient AI devices. Nirva addresses this by filtering out conversations from other people and recording only the wearer after an initial onboarding voice registration process. The device does not retain audio data or transcripts by default after processing.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: The company will start taking orders for the $249 device in November, aiming to ship to early users by the end of the year.

gist: Jobseekers worry about automated recruitment tools and bias.
Many workers are unaware they can request human reviews.
Recruiters note a surge in AI-written applications.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Jobseekers face automated rejections and growing concerns over AI recruitment tools. A campaign called Reject the Rejections highlights that many workers do not know their legal right to challenge automated decisions. Meanwhile, recruiters report a massive surge in applications, with many candidates using AI to polish or write their submissions.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Candidates fear recruitment software introduces bias and lacks human context. Surveys show that many ethnically diverse jobseekers alter their CVs out of fear of rejection. Conversely, recruiters note a perception gap, as candidates believe AI screens CVs far more often than it actually does.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Campaigners and regulators call for greater transparency, audits, and accountability from employers regarding automated hiring systems.

gist: Rio Ngumoha starred in Liverpool's 4-3 Champions League win over Villarreal.
The 18-year-old provided two crucial assists and won player of the match.
Head coach Andoni Iraola praised his development and attitude on the right flank.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Liverpool beat Villarreal 4-3 in the Champions League after trailing by two goals in the first half. sections.heading: Why it matters

gist: Emma Sing replaces Kildunne at full-back for the Red Roses.
Several personnel and positional changes are made following the defeat to Canada.
Sadia Kabeya starts while Alex Matthews moves to the bench.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Emma Sing comes in at full-back for Saturday's rematch against Canada in Ottawa. Tatyana Heard and Claudia Moloney-MacDonald drop out of the matchday squad entirely, replaced by Helena Rowland and Mia Venner. Sadia Kabeya starts after appearing off the bench last week, with Alex Matthews moving to the bench. Flo Robinson and Hollie Aitchison join the replacements.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The changes follow a defeat to Canada, with the coach noting the match is an opportunity to apply sustained pressure and learn from previous mistakes.

gist: Former rugby player Phil Vickery has taken up bodybuilding at 50.
He won the 2003 Rugby World Cup and earned 73 caps for England.
Vickery uses training to help manage his mental health and probable CTE diagnosis.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Phil Vickery competed in a bodybuilding show in Hull at the age of 50 after a challenge from a friend. He weighed about 99kg on stage, significantly lighter than his playing days.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Vickery has managed personal struggles and a diagnosis for probable CTE since retiring from rugby. Bodybuilding has provided him with discipline, a goal, and support for his physical and mental wellbeing.

fivew: Former rugby player Phil Vickery competed in a bodybuilding show.
To challenge himself and support his physical and mental fitness.

gist: Crystal Palace manager Pierre Sage felt shame after a 5-0 defeat by Brighton.
Sage admitted responsibility for the poor performance and said his future is uncertain.
Palace conceded three early goals in their heaviest loss to rivals Brighton since 1956.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Crystal Palace suffered a 5-0 defeat against Brighton after conceding three goals in the opening ten minutes. Manager Pierre Sage admitted responsibility for the performance, calling it his fault and stating he felt shame.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: Sage faces uncertainty regarding his job after a tough start following his summer appointment. The heavy loss was Palace's worst against their rivals since January 1956, leaving them with the most goals conceded in the top flight.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Crystal Palace travel to Turkey to play Besiktas in the Europa League on Thursday before hosting Newcastle in the Premier League on Sunday.

fivew: Sage took responsibility for the team's poor preparation and motivation.

gist: Celtic secured a seven to one victory against Hearts at Celtic Park.
Hearts suffered from severe defensive errors and psychological collapse during the match.
Celtic manager Martin O'Neill gained a much-needed win and praised his attacking players.

sections.heading: What happened
sections.text: Celtic defeated Hearts seven to one in a match featuring early goals and multiple defensive mistakes by the visitors.

sections.heading: Why it matters
sections.text: The emphatic win provides Celtic and manager Martin O'Neill with a significant boost after recent difficult periods.

sections.heading: What happens next
sections.text: Celtic aims to maintain this positive momentum over the long road ahead in the league campaign.
